items.title: Did You Hear That?
items.instructions: When you notice a gentle everyday sound outside, briefly describe it and make a quiet imitation. Give your child time to attend to the sound in their own way; a look or movement is enough. Do not repeatedly ask them to identify or reproduce it.

items.title: Sing-Song Voice
items.instructions: When your baby makes a sound, reply using a warm, gently musical voice. Pause to allow another response, or simply enjoy a short, quiet exchange. Watch their expression and continue only if they seem comfortable.

items.title: Sound Sensor
items.instructions: In a calm room, hum quietly or make a gentle familiar sound while your baby is awake. Watch whether they turn or shift their attention, and respond with a warm smile or a few words. The goal is a pleasant exchange, not a hearing test.

items.title: Look at a face
items.instructions: Bring your face into comfortable view and let your baby explore it visually. Your baby might look, turn, move, smile, make a sound, stay quiet or need a break. Any response is welcome; do not ask them to imitate or perform. Keep babies fully supervised and properly supported; never leave them on a raised changing surface. Pause when your child needs a break.

items.title: Slow visual tracking
items.instructions: While your baby is awake, slowly move a safe high-contrast object within comfortable view. Your baby might look, turn, move, smile, make a sound, stay quiet or need a break. Any response is welcome; do not ask them to imitate or perform. Use only intact age-suitable materials; no loose, detachable or mouth-sized pieces. Keep babies fully supervised and properly supported; never leave them on a raised changing surface. Pause when your child needs a break.

items.title: Observe and respond
items.instructions: Watch for signs that your baby is interested or needs a break and adjust play accordingly. Your baby might look, turn, move, smile, make a sound, stay quiet or need a break. Any response is welcome; do not ask them to imitate or perform. Keep babies fully supervised and properly supported; never leave them on a raised changing surface. Pause when your child needs a break.

items.title: Ready, Set, Play!
items.instructions: Look for your baby’s own signs of interest, such as looking towards you, making a sound or moving their arms. Respond by smiling, speaking or joining their chosen interaction, then pause to see what happens next. Stop when they signal that they need a break.

items.title: Responsive smile
items.instructions: Offer a warm smile during a calm face-to-face moment and allow time for a response. Your baby might look, turn, move, smile, make a sound, stay quiet or need a break. Any response is welcome; do not ask them to imitate or perform. Keep babies fully supervised and properly supported; never leave them on a raised changing surface. Never demand disclosure, apology, eye contact, physical touch or a particular emotional response. Pause when your child needs a break.

items.title: Body Language
items.instructions: Use a simple gesture while you speak, such as waving while saying hello or gently clapping while saying well done. Notice any comfortable response from your child, such as looking, moving, smiling, making a sound or using a gesture. Respond warmly; there is no need for the child to copy you.
